newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares close with small losses, dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares close with small losses, dull trade.

text.p: ** (1415 GMT) - Indian stocks finish shade lower in
lackustre trade, little action
** Bombay's benchmark 30-share index ends 7.86 points, or
0.21 percent lower at 3,754.51, off 3,780.34
** Markets seen consolidating at current price levels
** Foreign funds remain on the sidelines, show hesitancy
to buy stocks in big way, say traders
** National Stock Exchange 50-stock index falls 7.70
pts, or 0.72 pct, to finish at 1,066.50
** Delhi share index down 4.13 pts to 772.58, Calcutta 3.26
pts to 459.81, but Madras up 30.92 pts to 3,570.26
Blue-chip shares at major Indian bourses nudged lower in lacklustre trade on Thursday as fresh demand slowed, traders said.
"The markets have been pretty dull. Essentially, there is only trading activity," said Vetri Subramaniam, equity trader at Bombay institutional brokerage SSKI Securities Pvt Ltd.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's benchmark 30-share index drifted in a narrow band, ending 7.86 points lower at 3,754.51, off the intra-day high of 3,780.34.
"There seems to be some sort of consolidation-phase taking place," said Subramaniam.
The Bombay index rallied nearly 16 percent to hit an eight-month high of 4,029.56 last week, as participants welcomed a market-friendly budget announced by the government.

The 1997/98 (April-March) budget unveiled on February 28 proposed among other things a cut in corporate and personal income tax rates, raised foreign portfolio limit in domestic firms and allowed companies to buy back their shares.

But, profit-booking at higher levels capped the post-budget gains, dealers said. "Foreign funds and local institutions sold pivotals when the market was at the 4,000 level," said Neeraj Batra, president at Hinduja Finance.
Batra was confident about investment buying stepping in at lower levels. "A reaction of about 100-150 points, to the 3,600 levels will see fresh buying coming in," he said.

Shares of Castrol India surged 25.25 rupees, or 5.16 percent to close at 515.0 at the Bombay bourse with 560,694 shares traded. Dealers did not attribute any particular factor behind the surge despite some foreign fund buying seen in the stock.
Delhi shares closed lower on selling by foreign funds and Unit Trust of India, the nation's largest mutual fund, ahead of the end of the settlement on Friday, brokers said.
-- Anshuman Daga, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
